articleTitle: A new approach to integrated horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: As millimetre-wave systems are becoming increasingly important in many scientific and military applications, there is an increasing demand of various antennas for communications, radar or sensoring system. This is particular true for the research on short-range application such as local multipoint distribution system (LMDS), commercial airplane landing system used in low-visibility weather, automobile cruise control system and so on. Some recently developed integrated horn antennas showed attractive features in [1][2] for application mentioned above, nevertheless they are too expensive for widespread application.

articleTitle: Effects of Fresnel lens thickness on aperture efficiency
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of varying the thickness of a phase-correcting Fresnel lens on the mismatch losses at the air-dielectric lens interfaces in an attempt to improve the overall aperture efficiency. This approach is applied to a prototype lens designed at 30 GHz. A gain variation of more than 4 dB is observed as a function of lens thickness, leading to the conclusion that this parameter should not be overlooked in the design of phase-correcting Fresnel lenses.

articleTitle: Information theory and electromagnetism: Are they related?
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, we study the limitations imposed by the laws of electromagnetism on achievable MIMO channel capacity in its general form. Our approach is a two-fold one. First, we use the channel correlation argument to demonstrate that the minimum antenna spacing under any scattering conditions is at least half a wavelength. Secondly, using a plane-wave spectrum expansion of a generic electromagnetic wave combined with Nyquist sampling theorem in the spatial domain, we show that the laws of electromagnetism limit the minimum antenna spacing to half a wavelength, λ/2, (in the case of 1-D antenna apertures) only asymptotically, when the number of antennas n Å ∞. For a finite number of antennas, this limit is slightly less than λ/2. In any case, the number of antennas and, consequently, the MIMO capacity is limited for a given aperture size. This is a scenario-independent limit.

articleTitle: Time domain response of ultra wideband dipole antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Ultra Wideband (UWB) technology is defined as any wireless transmission scheme that occupies a −10 dB bandwidth of more than 20 percent of a center frequency, or more than 500 MHz. FCC has assigned a frequency range from 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz for operating UWB systems. In designing a UWB antenna, it is important to know the parameters such as the bandwidth for return loss below −10dB. It is also important to know what kind of time domain signals can be transmitted and received with minimum distortion, since the UWB antenna is meant to transmit or receive impulse signals. Even if a UWB antenna has a wide frequency bandwidth of matching, it does not guarantee the impulse signal would be received within such a frequency bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design and performance of a compact Ka-band communications and tracking feed chain
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In order to realize the high gains offered by multi-beam antennas, it is crucial to achieve a higher level of antenna pointing accuracy. Conventional 4-horn tracking clusters coupled to a tracking system allow to achieve good antenna pointing performance but these horn clusters are not well suited for combined communications and tracking operation. This paper presents the design and RF performance of a compact Ka-band multimode feed chain capable of supporting a high efficiency communications link while generating tracking signals for linearly or circularly polarized signals. The RF design is based on a very compact and modular concept. It incorporates up to three mode couplers to generate the required communications and tracking signals (TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>, and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode couplers) and uses a high-efficiency multimode horn to achieve optimal reflector illumination. Advanced, full wave modelling tools have been used to optimize the design. The performance of the combined tracking and communications feed chain was verified experimentally and the individual feed chain components were characterized in details. Excellent tracking and communications performance have been measured.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized 1-D EBG resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: We propose a circularly polarized resonator antenna made from a one-dimensional electromagnetic band gap (EBG) material. The antenna has the advantages of high gain, low losses and a low profile. A sequentially rotated array of linearly polarized stripline slots is used to generate circular polarization in the EBG resonator antenna. Preliminary theoretical results for this device and some details of the feed configuration are described.

articleTitle: A free-space measurement of complex permittivity of doped silicon wafers using transmission coefficient at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A contactless and non-destructive method is presented to characterize p-type and n-type silicon semiconductor wafers using a spot-focused free-space measurement system. In this method, the free-space reflection and transmission coefficients, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>, are measured for silicon wafer sandwiched between two teflon plates which are quarter-wavelength at mid-band. The actual reflection and transmission coefficient, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of the silicon wafers are then calculated from the measured S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> by using ABCD matrix transformation in which the complex permittivity and thickness of the teflon plates are known. Complex permittivity are computed using only the transmission coefficient, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>. From the complex permittivity, the resistivity and conductivity can be obtained. Results are reported in the frequency range of 9–12.5 GHz. The dielectric constant obtained were close to published values for silicon wafers and the resistivities agree well with that measured by other conventional method.

articleTitle: A reflectarray antenna in KA band with MEMS control
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A reflectarray antenna is an attractive solution for reconfigurable antennas, for it has both advantages of arrays — beam shaping with fixed antenna — and reflectors — high efficiency single feed. However, to be competitive, it has to present low losses, high reliability, and low cost.

articleTitle: Anik-F2 Ka-band transmit multibeam antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The design and RF performance of the Anik-F2 Ka-band Tx multibeam antenna is described. The antenna forms the transmit portion of the large multiple-beam antenna (MBA) farm installed on the Canadian Anik-F2 communication satellite. The antenna is required to generate 45 downlink spot beams to cover the North American continent. Stringent requirements of high EOC gain and high aggregate C/I pose challenges in the design. In order to meet these requirements, the design comprises four 55 inch offset parabola reflectors each illuminated by a separate feed cluster having high efficiency horns.

articleTitle: Optimization of microstrip tapered balun for sinuous antenna feeding circuits
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, we present optimization of microstrip tapered baluns that used in frequency independent antennas such as sinuous and spiral antennas. In this method, tapering profile of the baluns is optimized so that to achieve better matching results for input impedance of coaxial cable to balanced antenna input impedance with a shorter length of baluns. For this purpose we've used an optimized non-linear transducer where continuous variations in the transmission characteristics along it, provides an optimum balance-to-unbalance. Applicability of these baluns has been simulated with Ansoft HFSS. Measurement results for a dual polarized planar sinuous antenna in the 2–18GHz frequency range, exactly match with theory and simulation results.

articleTitle: The unconditionally-stable cycle-sweep method for 3D FDTD
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: To overcome the Courant limit in the explicit finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods, several unconditionally-stable methods have been proposed. This paper presents the cycle-sweep Crank-Nicolson method for solving 3D Maxwell's Equations. The cycle-sweep method is unconditionally stable and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order accurate in both time and space, and solves only six tridiagonal matrices instead of nine in the approximate-factorization-splitting method we reported previously. The cycle-sweep method is much more efficient than either a direct implementation of the Crank-Nicolson scheme or the approximate-factorization-splitting method.

articleTitle: On the limits of validity of the impedance boundary conditions for the analysis of induced currents in solid conductors
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The analysis of induced currents in conducting bodies due to the presence of an external magnetic field variable with time is necessary in numerous areas of applied electromagnetics, such as induction heating, eddy-current braking, electromagnetic shielding and electromagnetic levitation. An accurate study of the induced currents requires the field solution for both the inside and outside of the conductor. Exact analytical solutions are possible for a limited number of geometries. In order to reduce substantially the amount of computation, at high frequencies one can use the impedance boundary condition (IBC) models where only the field solution outside the conductor is needed. The simplest model is the perfect electrical conductor (PEC) model. More accurate results can be obtained by using the standard impedance boundary condition (SIBC) model and also the curvature corrected surface impedance models.

articleTitle: Synergy of fast antenna measurements and numerical modelling
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The correct performance evaluation of antennas operating in complex and electrically large environments such as satellites, ships, planes, mobiles etc. or antennas in urban or indoor environments, all require large and accurate measurement facilities, breadboarding of scaled models or complex on-site measurement campaigns. As a consequence, iterations during the design cycle based on antenna breadboard measurements or on-site performance verification of the final antennas are considered unfeasible by most antenna designers.

articleTitle: Operation of a periodic structure for a microstrip line over a large frequency band
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The operation of a microstrip transmission line with periodically-etched circles in the ground plane is investigated. The operation of the structure as a leaky-wave antenna is of particular interest. The structure is studied over a large frequency range, using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations.

articleTitle: Microwave power combining using the Talbot effect
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In the 1830s H.F. Talbot discovered the Talbot effect, also known as self or lensless imaging [1]. As shown in figure 1, this near-field effect allows that at specific distances, a grating under plane wave illumination yields exact copies of the one-or two-dimensional periodic grating pattern. The effect was observed under certain conditions when a beam of light was reflected from and/or transmitted through an amplitude or phase periodic structure.

articleTitle: Scattering analysis of an artificial dielectric composed of metallic disks with transversely modulated sizes
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The scattering characteristics of artificial dielectric made of a finite number of 2-D lattice planes of printed disks is analyzed based on the theory of dynamic interaction between small metallic disks and fields. The planar disk lattice has its disk size varying periodically in one direction (x) while remaining uniform in the other direction (y) to simulate a 1-D grating in effective permittivity. The transmitted and reflected fields under TE plane wave incidence are obtained in closed form and show that, beam switching can be achieved with the artificial dielectrics implemented in this way.

articleTitle: On the behavior of electromagnetic interference measured from glass insulator
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents the preliminary results of our investigation into the measurement of the spectrum generated by insulator under activity up to 31.6KV in normal weather conditions and artificial pollution. We use the classical antenna measurement technique to register the corona spectra. The results show a significant number of components in a large range of operating frequency. This encourages a deep study over a broad frequency range. The measurements were made in the HV laboratory using standard antenna. The range of measurements goes from 87MHz up to 900MHz. The amplitude levels of the EM spectrum from the isolator when compared with those from local radio station were very closed.

articleTitle: Analog tunable microwave phase shifters using RF MEMS
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: MEMS based microwave phase shifter designs are presented which give a continuously tunable, low loss voltage controlled phase shift. The device reported here offers a significant improvement over the circuits previously published. Measurements indicate that a 260 degree phase shift per centimeter is obtained at 30GHz, with a 90 degree phase shift per dB loss. This presents state of the art performance in analog MEMS tunable phase shifters.

articleTitle: H-plane waveguide filters with E-plane dispersive inverters for high-power applications
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Conventional H-plane waveguide filters are supplemented with E-plane stubs which simultaneously act as impedance inverters and create transmission zeros (attenuation poles) at prescribed frequencies. Due to the utilization of E-plane stubs, the filter can be manufactured as two identical halves joined in the center plane of the components. Since current in the housing is minimal in this plane, E-plane fabrication facilitates high-power applications. The different steps in the design of such filters are outlined. It is concluded that E-plane stub inverters are not only more compact than H-plane stubs but also display better return-loss behaviour. The individual designs are verified by independently developed and/or commercially available software packages.

articleTitle: Development of a dual band circularly-polarized cassegrain microstrip reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A design procedure and experimental results are presented for a high-gain dual-band, circularly-polarized (CP) reflectarray antenna with a Cassegrain feed, operating at Ku/Ka-band (Tx=30 GHz, Rx=20 GHz). The performance of this Cassegrain reflectarray antenna is compared with other CP reflectarray antennas designed by the authors of this paper. A transmit gain of 38 dBic and a received gain of 36 dBic with axial ratio of less than 2 dB for both bands was measured for this antenna.

articleTitle: Characterization of a transient wave reflected from a lossy half space using numerical inversion of laplace transform
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this article, one method based on numerical inversion of Laplace transform is applied to the transient analysis of the reflected wave from a conducting interface for both vertical and horizontal incidence. This method is applicable to any relative dielectric constant and incident angle, leads to good accuracy in both late and early time, and has a simple algorithm, short calculation time, small required memory size, readily controlled error and wide application range. Comparison between our results and the published results confirms the correctness and effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Controllable conformal electromagnetic band gap antenna for base station
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This work is a French Industry and Research project, called RNRT “BIP” (see ref.[1] for a presentation) and concern three University laboratories (IETR, IEF, GEA) and two societies (France Télécom, Adventen). The purpose of the RNRT project “BIP” is to design a beam steering multi-band (GSM/DCS/UMTS) base station antenna.

articleTitle: RF switch matrix interconnect network
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, a new integrated RF interconnect network is presented. The circuit is printed on a double sided alumina substrate, eliminating the need to use multilayer manufacturing technology. The interconnect network employs finite ground coplanar (FGC) lines and vertical 3-via transitions and can be easily integrated with semiconductor and MEMS switches to form a switch matrix. Simulation and experimental results are presented for a 3X3 interconnect network. The measured results show a return loss of −20 dB and an isolation of better than −40 dB up to 30 GHz.

articleTitle: A preliminary approach to simulate parallel mesh refinement with Petri nets for 3-D finite element electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: An approach utilizing Petri Nets for modeling and evaluating parallel, unstructured mesh refinement is developed. A model is implemented based on a detailed software prototype and system architecture, which mimics the behavior of the parallel meshing. Subsequently, estimates for performance measures are derived from discrete event simulations. The potential benefits and related costs of this new approach for developing high performance parallel mesh refinement algorithms are examined.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of a broadband near-field probe
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A technique for designing a broadband E-field probe is presented in this paper. Two versions of the probe balun are investigated, one using the original Marchand topology and a modified topology in which one pair of coupled lines is short-circuited to enhance low-frequency near-field coupling and reduce the size of the probe. The operation of the probe is validated experimentally using measurements over a simple test circuit. The results are compared with those from an active probe balanced with a differential amplifier. Balanced operation is demonstrated in the 100 MHz-2.5 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: CPW-fed DRA
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The CPW feed to the Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) has attracted considerable attention in view of the low loss, low dispersion and uniplanar nature of the CPW line compared to the microstrip feed [1]-[4]. Also, the CPW feed is easily amenable to active device integration without the need of vias. In view of the above, this paper illustrates three different configurations of CPW fed DRAs. In the first, the role of Electromagnetic Band-Gap (EBG) structures in the CPW ground plane and in the lower layer of the CPW substrate in increasing the F/B ratio and back-radiation performance is examined. Secondly, a circular polarized DRA is realized using a single coupled folded slot CPW feed. The third design illustrates the performance of CPW fed broadband Multisegment Dielectric Resonator Antenna (MSDRA). The advantages of the CPW feed over the microstrip feed to the MSDRA enhance the versatility and applicability of this antenna. Currently, simulated data on the above geometries using Ansoft's HFSS are presented. Fabrication and measurements of the above geometries are being conducted to verify the simulated results.

articleTitle: An autoregressive model for simulation of time-varying rain rate
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: An autoregressive (AR) model for computer generation of time-varying lognormally distributed rainfall rate is presented. The AR coefficients are derived from rain rate statistics and autocorrelation function obtained from measurement. Results from computer simulations are found to fit well with rain rate data from Barcelona.

articleTitle: Monopole intenna for Korea PCS mobile phone handset
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: We, in this paper, design and fabricate an intenna for the Korea PCS band (1.75–1.87GHz) handset terminal. Intenna design is based on the folded monopole theory, and has several hot spots to improve radiation performance in active state. Folding structure in antenna is performed to increase antenna impedance and effective height. Folding lines both near and far from feeding point make equivalently increasing of series capacitance, which has resonance to get broad bandwidth in spite of short length intenna. By measurements, 13.3%(1.75–1.99GHz) bandwidth at center frequency and −0.34dBi gain was achieved. This intenna has been applying in Samsung Korea PCS phone.

articleTitle: Elliptical cylinder dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Dielectric Resonators (DRs) have many applications as Microwave devices and Antenna. In many DRAs the simple geometry poses a significantly complex electromagnetic fields. There isn't analytical closed-form solution for most but hemispherical DRA. One usual method for the analysis of DRAs is finding propagation modes of its geometry and by knowing the location of feed approximate the mode or modes that propagate. Assuming that the boundaries are perfect magnetic conductors (PMC), tangential electric field components can be found on the walls and therefore far field pattern of antenna can be calculated [1]. To generate more accurate results we will combine PMC approximation with special green's function to analyze elliptical DR antennas.

articleTitle: Improving bandwidth of single layer diamond shape patch microstrip antenna with strip-via resonators
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The effect of rectangular strips with shorted vias on the bandwidth and radiation patterns of V-slotted diamond shape, single layer patch microstrip antenna is studied (Fig. 1). Its impedance bandwidth with linear polarization is increased from around 36 percent to 66% percent.

articleTitle: A new recursive approach for the full pattern reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The knowledge of the full three-dimensional radiation pattern of an antenna is mandatory for a proper use of it, as well as for an accurate evaluation of some parameters, such as its directivity. However, as well known, the antenna manufacturers make generally available only the patterns in the two principal planes. The half-power beamwidth in the vertical plane often replaces this last. The lack of information about the directional gain values outside the horizontal and vertical planes is today a very problem for the communication link designers. In fact, because of the distances existing in micro- and picocellular networks, the radiation direction from a base station of a mobile telephone system or from an access point of a wireless local area network (WLAN) can be very far from the principal planes. Accordingly, the simple use of the corresponding data gives rise to errors in the planning, so that a way for estimating the full three-dimensional radiation pattern is wanted. Note that the overestimation of the directional gain may lead to erroneous evaluations in the coverage planning, and that its underestimation can create interference problems. As a matter of fact, coverage and interference are usually analysed by using propagation models based on ray tracing, but comparisons between simulations and measurements often present discrepancies. These can depend on the model itself, but stem also from the approximation used for the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Tunable filters with a constant bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Today's microwave systems can benefit greatly from the use of tunable filters, which have some distinct advantages over traditional microwave filters and are continuously being improved. This paper presents an approach for designing tunable filters with a minimum number of tuning elements. While the majority of published work in this area uses synchronous tuning, the proposed approach is based on non-synchronous tuning.

articleTitle: An overview of the DRDC Ottawa RCS measurement system
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: As part of the continued requirement to characterize the radar signature of platforms of interests to the Canadian Forces, Defence R&D Canada (DRDC) maintains a capability to predict and measure the radar cross section (RCS) of various scatterers using a combination of analytical, numerical and experimental techniques. The inter-dependence between the three approaches remains important due to the complexity of electromagnetic scattering, as is the case when electrically large geometries are being considered. Indeed, structures on the scale of thousands of wavelengths such as ships at microwave frequencies are difficult to handle both numerically and experimentally. In particular, the large electrical dimensions of ships pose severe numerical challenges due to the prohibitive number of unknowns required; approximate high-frequency techniques must be used. Ship RCS measurements also pose challenges due to the logistics involved and the uncontrolled nature of the experiments. Furthermore, the sheer size of a naval vessel may also be problematic if one is interested in the far-field RCS since, properly speaking, such measurements may have to be carried out in the near field.

articleTitle: Mechanical considerations in antenna design
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Telecommunication providers require low cost, electrically and mechanically reliable products to satisfy customer requirements. In order to meet these expectations, antenna designers must venture beyond electrical performance into the realm of mechanical integrity and robustness. One of the main considerations when designing an antenna for a given commercial application is to classify the environment and the product lifetime in which the antenna is to operate successfully. Antenna applications such as cellular, GSM, PCS, DECT, WLL/WLAN, rural point-to-multipoint, and digital audio broadcast antennas require normal operation in an outdoor environment which may see extremes in temperature, humidity, altitude, ice, snow, rain and wind. The designer must first define the worst case operating conditions that the antenna is expected to meet, and then ensure the antenna design exceeds these specifications. In accomplishing this task, the designer will employ as many tools that they have at their disposal. These tools include hand calculations, 3D computer aided design (CAD) packages, Finite Element Analysis (FEA), standard environmental specifications, standard test procedures, and rapid prototype printing. Every effort must be made to ensure collaboration between electrical and mechanical aspects of a design early on in the concept phase of a new product to ensure success.

articleTitle: Copper coplanar waveguides on Si substrates for frequencies up to 40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study of copper coplanar waveguides fabricated on silicon substrates suitable for use in post-process CMOS IC fabrication. The waveguides were separated from the substrate by thick layers of polyimide. Waveguide performance is compared to that of aluminum control devices underlayed with silicon dioxide. The lower resistance of the copper and improved substrate isolation obtained with the low-k polyimide dielectric provide a significant performance boost compared to the controls. Application of the copper/polyimide waveguides in a 10 GHz distributed amplifier in 0.35 μm CMOS technology is examined. A significant performance advantage is observed for the Cu/Polyimide CPWs compared to Al/SiO2 controls.

articleTitle: Si monolithic antenna calibration and de-embedding considerations
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an integrated balun for testing 24 GHz on-chip differential antennas. The balun is completely characterized on lossy Si substrate for subsequent de-embedding of the antenna impedance. A simple de-embedding technique is developed and verified to extract differential antenna impedance from single-ended S-parameters. The gain of the on-chip antennas is estimated through a novel gain calibration technique.

articleTitle: Phase shifter using defected ground structures with MEMS actuated cavity backing
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A MEMS-based control structure consisting of a flexible membrane to actuate ground plane defects is presented. Initial tests were performed with a manually constructed cavity structure placed behind the slot. The cavity depth is increased in discrete intervals and the phase difference determined. Promising results from this experiment led to the application of the membrane itself beneath the ground plane defect. The membrane-backed design allows a continuous generation of phase shift through the variation of the cavity depth. An electrode below the membrane causes a deflection due to an applied electrostatic force, allowing a cavity to form between the membrane and the defect in the ground plane. These cavity-backed designs add negligible loss to the system.

articleTitle: Investigations of far-field phase shift of wideband rectangular microstrip antenna for phased array applications
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents the investigation results on Far-field phase shift of an E-shape wide band rectangular microstrip antenna for phased array applications. Substrate thickness variation is used for generating the phase shift. Effect of other antenna design parameters were also studied, but showed less influence. A Far-field phase shift of around 180° was achieved with an air gap thickness variation of 4.00 mm from the initial height. In three element phased array implementation, this provided 20° of beam scan. This type of phase shifter may be implemented using Micro-Electro-Mechanical technology.

articleTitle: Compact antenna design and analysis for collision avoidance radar at 76 GHz
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Collision avoidance radar systems will become standard equipment on vehicles in the near future. Their purpose is to adjust the distance between vehicles and/or alert the driver when dangerous situations arise. Usually located behind the front bumper, these systems need a compact antenna with high gain, to achieve a long-range detection at 76 GHz. As specifications require high gain, electrically large focusing elements are required. Therefore, the design technique proposed is based on Geometrical Optics (GO). Radiation field patterns of various proposed structures are compared to other techniques such as Method of Moments (MoM), Physical Optics (PO) and measurement. It is found that GO gives some reasonably good results for a fast design.

articleTitle: Single boundary integral equation for static fields in the presence of penetrable bodies
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Laplacian electrostatic fields in the presence of dielectric bodies are usually analyzed using an integral equation for the density of the polarization charge over their surfaces. The advantage of this equation consists in its computational efficiency for systems of homogeneous bodies and in that the potential and the field intensity are calculated everywhere by employing elementary Coulombian formulas. In this paper, however, a single-source boundary integral equation is derived using the Green representation of the potential outside the dielectric bodies, a single surface source representation of the potential inside the bodies, and applying the boundary conditions. The formulation presented is important since it can easily be extended to structures containing layered bodies to derive a boundary integral equation substantially more efficient than the existent equations. Based on field analogies, the results obtained for electrostatic fields can directly be translated for other static fields in the presence of penetrable bodies.

articleTitle: Implementation of the circuit showing the characteristics of the double negative materials
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In 1968, Veselago proposed the material that had simultaneously negative permittivity ε and permeability μ, which means ε < 0 and μ < 0 [1], and hence, this material has been called as double negative (DNG) material [2]. Veselago proved its unusual characteristics which does not exist in nature, such as a negative refractive index (NRI), negative wave vector k, negative group velocity v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, left-handed set (k, E, H), backward-wave (k is anti-parallel to Poynting vector S), and negative group velocity v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>. After about three decades, periodic structures comprised of split-ring resonators [3] and conductive strips have been developed by Smith [4] and verified as having a NRI and negative group velocity within very narrow band around resonant frequency [5], but being lossy. Other approaches using series capacitors and shunt inductors (C-L configuration) [6] have been extensively studied by Itoh [7] and Eleftheriade's groups [8]. Theses C-L networks having NRI are broad band and low loss, but do not provide the negative group velocity of Veselago's DNG material, which is discussed later. Recently, Mojahedi's group [9] has proposed a transmission line made of the C-L configuration and the embedded RLC resonator circuits that has presented a NRI and negative group velocity, but heavily mismatched and lossy because of its embedded resistor.

articleTitle: Field of a large circular loop antenna around a conducting sphere
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The electromagnetic field of a circular loop antenna of radius a, carrying a nonuniform current I(ϕ), in the presence of a conducting sphere of radius b<a located symmetrically is considered. The current distribution on the thin-wire circular loop driven by a delta-function generator is determined by a Fourier series expansion in terms of tesseral harmonics. Eigenfunction series solutions for the field are assumed in different regions. The unknown coefficients are computed by enforcing boundary conditions at the interfaces of these different regions. Field components are obtained analytically in closed form and field patterns are plotted for various cases.

articleTitle: Optimum beam forming of LEO satellite antenna with genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In LEO satellite communications, each earth station observes the satellite only in short periods of time, in different directions with different slant ranges [1]. The purpose of this design is to create a link with fixed received signal level in different times and consequently independency of bit rate from the elevation angle. To compensate higher path losses for low elevation angles antenna's directivity in corresponding angles should be increased. In this way, in earth receivers antennas with hemispherical radiation pattern could be used without the tracking system.

articleTitle: Fresnel zone plate antenna analysis using artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Analysis of the Fresnel Zone Plate Antenna (FZPA) towards optimum design is presented using artificial neural network (NN). To this purpose, the diameter and focal length of FZPA are the inputs, and maximum gain and optimum illumination factor of the feed are the outputs of the neural network.

articleTitle: Microstrip log periodic antenna (LPA) using inset feed
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The fabrication and simulation of the inset feed log periodic antenna has been investigated with four different numbers of elements: five, seven, nine and eleven. The antennas have been modeled using microstrip lines and S parameter data from single element. The data is extracted from the momentum simulation and combined with the microstrip transmission line. The properties of antennas such as bandwidth, gain, cross-polar isolation and half power beamwidth have been investigated and compared between different elements.

articleTitle: Folding high frequency substrate for interference mitigation in active antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Printed circuit board antennas are often designed to incorporate active elements such as high power amplifiers in order to boost the EIRP of the antenna [1]. Active devices however generate heat. Thus it becomes necessary to employ cooling mechanisms to ensure proper operation of the active antenna. For most applications heat sinks are used for cooling. The drawback of using heat sinks however is that its fins are metallic, which can potentially lead to interference with the radiation pattern. A possible active array implementation is shown in Figure 1 [2]. This paper discusses a novel implementation of conformal antennas, whereby the high frequency substrate is folded, to reduce any unwanted coupling between the radiating elements and the heatsink fins.

articleTitle: Infinitesimal dipoles simulation of antennas using genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Infinitesimal dipoles are used to simulate some antennas. The Genetic Algorithm (GA) method is used to minimize the near field difference of the antenna and the field from certain number of infinitesimal dipoles of arbitrary orientation. The obtained dipoles from single frequency measurements are found to be valid for certain frequency band.

articleTitle: Broadband stacked printed antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas have the attractive features of low profile and light weight, and can be made conformal to mounting structures. The conventional patch antennas suffer from the narrow bandwidth. To overcome this problem, a two layer electromagnetically coupled rectangular patch antenna is considered in this paper. A T-shaped probe fed rectangular patch stackeded by another parasitic one is considered. A wide impedance bandwidth (SWR ≤ 2) of 60% and a gain of about 9 dB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> are achieved. The measured published results of the single element are conformed and then the radiation characteristics of the stacked antenna are investigated using IE3D software.

articleTitle: Substrates characterisation (ε r, tg δ) up to millimeter wavelength
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The development of applications in millimetre waves domain is very important in the last years. For example, many studies have been done for indoor communications at 60 GHz, spatial communications in Q band (50 GHz), radar automotive applications (77 GHz). Microstrip technology should be attractive at these frequencies if one uses material with weak losses and a low cost technology. The most of substrates are always well known up to 10 GHz in term of dielectric permittivity and loss tangent but it's more difficult to obtain information about theses parameters in millimeter wave range. Then, when printed antennas for example are studied, it becomes primordial to do substrates characterisation in millimeter waves, if we want good agreement between theory and experiment in term of antenna resonant frequency for example. In this paper, the authors use a very simple method to obtain εr and tgδ and give results about these parameters for different substrates. This last method using a printed resonator stub is compared using several examples with well known methods like free space and High Q Fabry Perrot cavity techniques.

articleTitle: Effects of dimple geometry on RF MEMS switch heating
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents the effects of the size and location of the contact dimples on the heating of RF MEMS cantilever contact switches. The analyses are based on electromagnetic model with the extended finite element-boundary integral (EFE-BI) method, integrated with thermal model with the finite element (FE) method. Simulation results demonstrate that larger dimples result in lower contact temperature, suggesting the higher power delivery capability of the dimples with a large contact area.

articleTitle: Synthesizing an incident aperiodic tapered beam
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents a technique for generating numerically an amplitude tapered incident plane wave of a prescribed polarization and a prescribed incidence by summing a finite number of propagating uniform plane waves. This work is a continuation of the work presented in [1] where an oblique 2D-periodic beam was synthesized. Here, the 2D-periodic beam is synthesized for normal incidence, then it is made aperiodic by windowing the spatial distribution to a single cell with the use of a box function. Then the resulting beam is rotated to the prescribed incidence by carrying out a coordinate transformation. Finally, the spectrum distribution is thresholded to confine the constellation of constituent plane waves to the main lobe of the spectrum function.

articleTitle: Effects of reflector size and spacing on microstrip slot antenna performance
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Microstrip slot antennas in the presence of a reflector is studied. The reflector is used to obtain unidirectional radiation pattern. Effects of reflector parameters, e.g. reflector spacing, reflector width and length are studied. Even with the reflector, the microstrip slot antenna shows a wide bandwidth of about 65.7%, with good front-to-back ratio. Excellent impedance matching can be achieved by selecting proper reflector size and spacing.

articleTitle: Wavelet decomposition applied to radar technology
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A modern approach to radar target recognition and identification based on wavelet decomposition of the Radar Cross Section is presented. The application of this technique in radar technology for both simple and complex targets recognition is then numerically investigated. Results obtained show that this technique is very promising and yields recognition levels difficult to achieve with any other currently available technique.

articleTitle: A receive-mode analysis of reflectarray antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: It is known that with conventional paraboloidal reflector antennas there are situations when maximum directivity is achieved with the feed displaced from the geometrical focal point, either slightly toward or away from the reflector [1]. This apparent shift of the true focal point is informatively revealed by considering the reflector in a receive-mode analysis. A plane wave is considered incident on the reflector along its axis, and the scattered field is computed as a function of position on the reflector axis [2]. In this paper we study focal shifts in reflectarray antennas. In addition, for plane wave incidence on such reflectarrays, we interpret the focal region fields in terms of Gaussian beams.

articleTitle: Decreasing the quality factor of an electrically small electric dipole through an increase in effective volume
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Electrically small antennas are generally presumed to exhibit high impedance mismatch (high VSWR), low efficiency and high quality factor (Q); and therefore narrow operating bandwidth. For an electric or magnetic dipole antenna there is a fundamental lower bound for the quality factor, which is determined as a function of the antenna's maximum physical dimensions [1]. In this work, the quality factor of an electrically small electric dipole is reduced through an increase in the antenna's effective volume. A self-resonant, electrically small electric dipole antenna is presented that exhibits an impedance near 50 Ohms, an efficiency in excess of 95% and a quality factor that is within 1.5 times the fundamental lower bound at ka less than 0.27.

articleTitle: Transmission line phase shifters using defected ground structures
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Explorations into the domain of electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures have become increasingly common in recent years. By etching these structures into a circuit ground plane, they have been applied within the planar microstrip medium for use as filters at microwave and millimetre-wave frequencies. They have been effective within system designs in the suppression of undesirable harmonics, as well as within antenna applications to achieve improved radiation characteristics through loss suppression. However, their slow-wave properties have not been exploited to a large extent with regard to their impact on realizing a phase variation. These structures can be used to realize more compact phase shifter designs, while adding virtually no additional losses to the system.

articleTitle: Broadband folded printed quadrifilar helical antenna with wide arms
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: With the development of the satellite communication systems (GPS, INMARSAT), the Printed Quadrifilar Helical Antennas (PQHA) have found wide applications due to its features of circular polarization, good axial ratio and its low cost. Nevertheless, they suffer from their narrow bandwidth (5 ∼ 8%), which could be insufficient for such applications.

articleTitle: A tapered short helical antenna radiating a circularly polarized tilted beam
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) wave radiation beam tilted from the direction normal to an antenna plane can be obtained using spiral [1][2] and loop antennas [3]. However, little theoretical analysis for the tilted beam from a helical antenna has been performed. This paper fills this gap and a CP tilted beam is obtained using a tapered short helical antenna. The frequency responses of the axial ratio and gain in the beam direction, together with the input impedance, are calculated and discussed.

articleTitle: Performance of multimode (TE11+TE21) feed horn for offset reflector antenna providing multiphase centres
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The phase centre of a feed horn is a theoretical point along the axis of the horn which is the centre of curvature of the phase fronts of the spherical waves. In most feeds, there is a phase centre region rather than a single point because radiation is due to a summation of spherical waves, which seems to emanate from the aperture [1]. Determination of the feed phase centre helps, its location relative to the focal point of the reflector. Different techniques to compute and determine the phase centre location in single and dual reflector geometries are reported in [1-3]. However, when the feed horn has a multimode excitation, the amplitude and phase control of modes provide different constant phase centre locations, which in turn helps to conceptualize a virtual array on the reflector antenna aperture [4].

articleTitle: Fast transient analysis of incident field coupling to multiconductor transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for fast transient analysis of multiconductor transmission line interconnects in the presence of incident fields. In the proposed approach: (a) The formulation of equivalent external sources due to incident fields is independent of the type of the macromodel used to represent the MTL system and can be represented analytically in the time-domain solely based on the information of per-unit-length parameters of the line and incident field parameters, (b) An efficient passive macromodel based on delay extraction and closed-form representation is used to describe the distributed nature of the MTL stamp. The time-domain macromodel is in the form of ordinary differential equations and can be easily included in SPICE like simulators for transient analysis. The proposed algorithm, while guaranteeing the stability of the simulation by employing passive macromodels, provides significant speed-up for transmission line networks, especially with large delay and low-losses.

articleTitle: GPR target detection using a neural network classifier of image moments as invariant features
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Preliminary results of automatically detecting unexploded ordinance (UXO) and landmines using an artificial neural network (ANN) to classify particular features in a ground penetrating radar (GPR) image are given. These features are the so-called invariant moments of a GPR image. The automatic detection algorithm is described and results of experiments conducted for both metal and dielectric targets buried in a sandbox are provided. Currently, only metallic targets can be discriminated by the ANN with many false negative indications occurring.

articleTitle: Electric fields in tissue from gradient coils in MRI
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Magnetic fields associated with gradient switching in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) systems produce electric fields. In the case of fast switching fields of high magnitude, peripheral nerves stimulation (PNS) may occur [1], [2]. Several research groups have conducted investigations of PNS in human subjects, e.g. [1]-[9]. The stimulation threshold expressed as a function of the time derivative of the magnetic flux density, dB/dt, depends on the duration of the rectangular stimulus (pulse width) At, and can be described as [10].

articleTitle: Electric dyadic green's function for unbounded gyromagnetic medium
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Propagation and radiation of electromagnetic waves in anisotropic media are problems of great interest from both theoretical and practical points of view. For the problems of radiation and scattering from sources embedded in stratified media, one of the most powerful and elegant analyzing tools is the dyadic Green's function (DGF) technique. Many researchers have determined and utilized the DGF for planarly multi-layered media. Some of the methods used to find Green's functions for the multi-layered problems include Fourier-transform domain representations with matrix analysis techniques and plane wave spectral representations of the DGFs with vector wave functions. As technology of material science advances, more complex new materials are manufactured for a variety of applications. This trend leads to the growing interest in obtaining the corresponding DGF for studying these materials in detail. For a given set of sources, the field may be easily found if the DGF of the medium is available. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that once the expansions of unbounded DGF are available, the layered-media DGF can be formulated readily.

articleTitle: Modeling of materials with negative refractive index using TLM 3D SCN node and inter-cell networks
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper we describe the modeling of materials with negative refractive index (metamaterials) using the transmission line matrix (TLM) 3D SCN node in combination with inter-cell networks. The 3D TLM representation of metamaterials, its implementation, and simulation results computed with this representation will be presented.

articleTitle: A novel single surface integral equation for the analysis of fields in the presence of induced solid conductors
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Quasistationary fields in the presence of solid conductors can be analysed by using coupled boundary integral equations (BIE) which are formulated in terms of two unknown quantities over each conductor surface. These unknowns can be either the magnetic vector potential and its normal derivative [1] or the conduction current density and its normal derivative [2], or the equivalent surface electric and magnetic currents [3]. In a previous paper, we formulated a single-source surface integral equation (SSSIE) satisfied by a single unknown current density distributed over the surface of the conducting bodies, thus reducing by half the number of unknowns and decreasing significantly the CPU time [4]. The vector potential inside the conductors was expressed in terms of a single surface electric current density, while the potential outside was obtained from the formula of three potentials for Laplacian fields.

articleTitle: Beam shaping of Yagi-Uda antenna using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: To obtain the best achievement when facing an antenna optimization problem, the first step is to choose a suitable model. Although, usually the design parameters in an antenna problem are some specific parameters such as Gain, VSWR, SLL or Bandwidth, in some cases it is needed to optimize a set of parameters simultaneously such as a beam shaping problem. These kinds of problems, which are mostly found in radars [1], wireless [2] and satellite [3] communications, could be optimized using evolutionary algorithms.

articleTitle: Matlab-based accurate dispersion models for unshielded suspended microstrip
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Suspended microstrip, shown in Fig.1 (unshielded case) and Fig. 2 (shielded case), is a very useful variation of the conventional microstrip structure. This transmission line is created by introducing an air-gap between the ground plane and the substrate, as shown in Figs. 1 and 2. The main advantages of this type of microstrip, over the conventional microstrip, follow.

articleTitle: A novel adaptive algorithm for antenna arrays CDMA mobile communications systems
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This contribution presents a modified On-Off algorithm for adaptive antenna arrays employed at base stations of CDMA communication systems. Two algorithms are proposed: one with a fixed step size (F-On-Off) and a second one with a variable step size (V-On-Off). Using a geometric-based stochastic channel model, numerical simulations were carried out to perform comparisons between the F-On-Off, and V-On-Off algorithms. Numerical results were provided to evaluate the performance of the proposed approaches with the RAKE receiver. Simulations suggest that the F-On-Off performance is viable and allows an improvement of the system capacity.

articleTitle: Smart antenna for capacity enhancement of wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The use of a smart antenna is a major step forward in a cellular system. In existing deployments, smart antennas must be integrated with conventional cell site equipment to function as an adaptive spatial filter that yields increased signal quality, capacity, and/or range over conventional antennas. Such an implementation requires a combination of active microwave and digital electronics as an integral part of its system. This paper therefore explores areas of strategic importance in integration of new antenna array topologies which are appropriated for use as a building block for the indoor wireless system.

articleTitle: W3A top floor antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper design and RF performance of the W3A Top Floor Antenna is described. The antenna combines two dual gridded Ku-band reflector antennas and a Ka-band Gregorian antenna on single tower. Very stringent performance requirements with respect to the antenna EOC gain, XPD and low PIM at 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order, have been imposed. The mechanical design of the W3A antenna was also very challenging due to its very large size and complexity. Very good RF performance for all three antennas was achieved.

articleTitle: Aperture coupled dielectric resonator antennas for dual frequency applications
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) are highly suitable for applications in mobile and wireless communication systems owing to their many attractive features, such as high radiation efficiency, different available feeding mechanisms, flexibility over a large frequency range, light weight, small and compact size, and larger bandwidth capabilities. Recently, many investigations have been reported on DRA multi-frequency operations using some approaches, including loading additional structures (dielectric materials or metal stripes), or combining multiple resonators [1]-[4]. However, these approaches increase the size and the weight of DRAs and lead to complex fabrication process. To overcome this limitations, a novel structure for dielectric resonator antenna is proposed to achieve a dual frequency operation and to improve some antenna characteristics. The proposed antenna designs are described and measured results are presented.

articleTitle: A miniaturized ring resonator using a left-handed transmission line section
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel miniaturized ring resonator configuration that employs a combination of right-handed and left-handed transmission lines. It is shown that combining right-handed and left-handed transmission lines can result in a miniaturized resonator configuration whose resonant frequency is independent of its length. The proposed concept allows the realization of considerably smaller resonators in comparison with traditional ring resonators. Moreover, it offers a remarkable wide spurious free window. In practice, the maximum miniaturization of the proposed ring resonator is limited by the maximum achievable capacitance and inductance per unit area. The proposed concept can also be extended to other planar resonator configurations. Practical considerations to realize these structures are also discussed.

articleTitle: Using reciprocity to synthesize an incident aperiodic tapered beam
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents the use of the reciprocity principle and the near-to-far field transformation for synthesizing an incident tapered beam of a prescribed polarization and a prescribed incidence. The tapered beam can be either Maxwellian or non-Maxwellian. The Maxwellian beam is synthesized by summing a finite number of propagating plane waves whose polarizations are chosen judiciously. The non-Maxwellian beam is generated analytically by assigning a Gaussian profile and a uniform polarization to the field distribution. It turns out that the use of the reciprocity principle and the near-to-far field transformation works very well for the Maxwellian beam but not very well for the non-Maxwellian beam.

articleTitle: Using the Laguerre polynomials to get a stable solution of TD-EFIE for thin-wire antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Time domain electrical field integral equation (TD-EFIE) technique has been proven to be an effective and convenient tool for time domain analysis of various electromagnetic problems [1-4]. It has been applied to many scattering and radiation problems. The most popular method to solve a TD-EFIE is the marching-on in time (MOT) method using triangular patches and vector basis functions proposed by Rao, Wilton and Glisson (RWG) [5]. However, as pointed by many researchers, the TD-EFIE with the MOT method may suffer from its late-time instability. Much work has been done to eliminate the instability [6-11]. Some of them can get satisfactory results, but it may cost more computer time.

articleTitle: Broadband printed monopole antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Microstrip patch antenna is generally the most popular antenna for portable devices. These antennas however are inherently narrow band. To obtain a wide bandwidth form a microstrip patch antenna the substrate thickness has to be increased and the dielectric constant of the substrate has to be kept as low as possible [1]. Long feed probes required for antennas with thick substrates introduce undesirable inductive effects. Novel feed methods such as L probe feeds and F probe feeds have been reported in [2] and [3], respectively, to eliminate such effects. In addition, as reported in [2] and [4], slot loading of the patch antenna has been successfully employed in enhancing the bandwidth. Another broadband antenna, designed for a thin substrate, includes a rectangular slot inside a rectangular metal patch [5].

articleTitle: Parametric study of multibeam MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, we investigated the performance of a linear uniform array, as it is usually used in the Multi-Input-Multi-Output (MIMO) systems. By using the Phased Array (PA) techniques we investigated the effect of pattern rotation on the system capacity. We introduce a new approach to realize maximum achievable capacity through pattern diversity by using multi-beam phased array antenna. The ray-tracing method was used to simulate the system performance in a realistic propagation environment. The initial results showed more than 98%, 92% and 83% of the theoretical capacity limit could be achieved when the number of transmitter and receiver antennas are respectively (2,2), (3,3) and (4,4).

articleTitle: A wide-band compact planar antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Patch antennas offer several advantages in many practical applications, among them wireless communication. The main limitation of a classical patch is a very narrow bandwidth. In recent years several modifications have been introduced to the patch design aimed at increasing impedance bandwidth and gain without increasing the patch size [1]-[14]. Short-circuiting the patch, introduction of slots, substrate of low dielectric constant, closely coupled elements forming a patch and thick substrate have been used. A modification of the ground plane by holes and slots is not considered as viable here, as it results in considerable back radiation. While by increasing overall antenna dimensions the impedance bandwidth can be reasonably increased, maintaining a compact structure presents an additional challenge.

articleTitle: Aperture area enhancement in circularly polarized microstrip patch arrays using square patches with shorting pins
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Circular polarization has always been very effective for many radio systems, such as communications, remote sensing, navigation and radar systems. In these systems, it is desirable for the ground terminal to have a low-profile and lightweight antenna. Additionally, high gain, electronic beam scanning, beam shaping, and low sidelobe-radiation patterns are often required [1]. Microstrip patch arrays satisfy all of the above requirements along with low cost of fabrication. Circular polarization in microstrips is achieved by different methods some of which include: use of multiple feeds, corner feeds, tilted slot placed on the element, elliptical patch element, square patch with slanted corners, circular patch with perturbations, etc. In these methods, two orthogonal modes of equal amplitude and a differential phase of ±90° degrees are excited. In this paper, circularly polarized arrays with shorted metallic patches (SMP) placed in the vicinity of the radiating element are studied. It is shown that the implementation of the SMP in a four element array can have significant improvements on the gain as well as the matching of the elements. All the results have been simulated on infinite ground using Ansoft Ensemble 8.

articleTitle: Adjoint sensitivities of real objective functions for time-domain TLM
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: We review the Adjoint Variable Method (AVM) for efficient estimation of real objective function sensitivities with time-domain TLM. The original electromagnetic structure is first simulated using TLM. An adjoint TLM simulation that runs backward in time is derived and solved. The sensitivities of the objective function with respect to all designable parameters are estimated using only the original and adjoint simulations. The AVM approach is illustrated through the estimation of the sensitivities of objective functions with respect to the dimensions of waveguide discontinuities.

articleTitle: Simulation of transients on frequency dependent transmission lines using an improved multipoint Padé approximation technique
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Transmission line structures are commonly found in electrical power delivery systems. Efficient transient simulations of transmission line networks are important for characterization of power system performance. Conventionally, transients on power transmission lines are computed using time domain techniques such as PSCAD simulator [1] and the computational effort associated is generally high. In the last decade, model order reduction techniques, such as multipoint Padé approximation method, have been introduced for the analysis of interconnect networks containing transmission lines and have demonstrated a high computational efficiency as compared to conventional circuit simulation methods [2]-[5]. Multipoint Padé approximation method employs all moment sets available at all updated frequency expansion points and can be used to efficiently obtain a closed-form solution of the linear networks in the presence of distributed transmission line models. Despite its success in solving interconnect circuit problems, applications of multipoint Padé approximations to transients simulation of power transmission lines are not always straightforward. This is because transmission lines in power systems are generally high frequency dependent as compared to those found in typical high-speed interconnect circuits, resulting in solution instability of multipoint Padé approximations. More specifically, the matrix that is used to yield coefficients of Padé rational transfer function is prone to be ill-conditioned when multipoint Padé approximation method is applied to simulate frequency dependent power transmission lines.

articleTitle: A new methodology for substrate network resistance extraction in RFCMOS
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper substrate network resistances are analyzed and extracted for multi-finger MOS transistors used in RF applications. The commonly used model for MOS transistors in RF applications mainly consists of a substrate resistance network having three resistors. A typical horse-shoe CMOS transistor laid out and all substrate resistances are extracted from I-V characteristics. Device and process simulation results for 0.25μm CMOS technology show that the horse-shoe structure decreases the parasitic substrate resistance by 27%. Additionally, we show that the results obtained from traditional approximation method deviated about 31% from the exact results. Furthermore, with proposed method, the substrate resistance values can be exactly extracted.

articleTitle: Performance of microstrip phase shifter implemented using ground plane slot structures
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Beam steering in phased arrays is normally achieved using RF phase shifters [1]. They provide inter-element phase shifts, independent of the other system components, in the form of insertion phase delays. Consequently, they also introduce insertion loss in the process. The magnitude of the loss is dependent on the phase shifter type and generally increases with frequency. Many types of phase shifters have been studied in past years including Ferrite and solid-state phase shifters [2]. In recent years, several groups have investigated micro-electro-mechanical-systems (MEMS) switch based phase shifters [3]. MEMS based phase shifters can offer a high phase shift at very low series resistance. A new type of phase shifter formed from a reconfigurable microstrip structure, using MEM copper membranes distributed in the ground plane below the transmission line was presented in [4].

articleTitle: Stability considerations of an active integrated dielectric grating antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A method for determining stability of an active antenna is presented with some simulation results. The gain margin is greater than 3dB over a 40GHz bandwidth for the active antenna that we present here.

articleTitle: Far-field characterisation of large arrays: A methodical approach
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The work described in this paper is being carried out within the framework of two successive projects called SANTANA I & II (Smart Antenna Terminal) [1], funded by the German government (BMBF) on behalf of the DLR. The goal of these projects is the realisation of a demonstrator of a certain type of phased array, for applications such as terminals for broadband satellite communication (figure 1). This type of terminal can provide a link between airplanes and GEO satellites, for example.

articleTitle: Analysis of effect of radiation of an external wave on a bended microstrip line
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper analysis of effect of radiation of an external electromagnetic wave on a lossless bended microstrip line will be discussed. The method of analysis of this paper is based on Quasi-TEM wave propagation in microstrip lines. By applying circuit equivalent model of this transmission line and the bend and induced voltage and current sources in it, distributed voltage and current on the microstrip was calculated.

articleTitle: Extracting causal time domain parameters
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Parameters of a device are normally given in a frequency range of interest. To use them in a time-domain simulator requires their time-domain correspondents to be strictly causal in time. However, these time-domain correspondents are often non-causal in time if they are obtained from simple transformations of the frequency-domain parameters known over a limited frequency-range of interest. In this paper, a simple technique is presented that uses the iterative approaches. The usefulness of the technique is demonstrated by removing noncausal aspects of a set of measured Y-parameters of a FET transistor.

articleTitle: Directivity computation of radio base station antennas via cylindrical NF-FF transformation
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: As well known, the directivity value associated to a radiating system denotes its capacity to concentrate the electromagnetic radiation in a desired direction.
