The computation of the total radiated power, which is obtained by integrating the radiation intensity on the far field (FF) spherical surface, represents the crucial point in the directivity evaluation. The full numerical integration can be used to this end only in numerical simulations, and becomes very time consuming when the computation of the radiation intensity is onerous, as in the case of electrically large antennas. An efficient Sampling Interpolation (SI) formula for determining the total radiated power from the knowledge of a nonredundant number of the radiation intensity samples has been proposed in [1]. It is in closed form, does not depend on the type of antenna under test (AUT) and allows one to efficiently estimate the directivity from simulated or measured samples with a very significant reduction of the number of data with respect to [2].

articleTitle: Methods for determining capacity in an alternate mode of optical data storage
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Current data storage techniques are based on magnetic and optical technologies such as hard drives and compact discs (CDs) respectively. Research in magnetic technologies has achieved data densities of 100 Gbits/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (∼15 Gbits/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)[1]. With the more recent discovery of optical data storage research has greatly improved data densities with implementations such as the DVD that consists of multiple layers of CDs and Blu-Ray technology that uses a shorter wavelength optical source to decrease the feature size and increase data density up to 2 Gbits/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Although research continues to improve these technologies, both magnetic and optical data storage are limited in their readout speeds due to their serial readout nature.

articleTitle: Recursive MVDR for direction finding using circular arrays
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Digital beamforming is one of the important topics in wireless communication systems. The goal of beamforming is to detect the arriving angles of various sources such that the direction of arrivals (DOA) for different signals can be determined for further process. For direction finding, traditional minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamformer provides a straightforward approach in solving this problem. The approach of MVDR is based on optimum filtering and spectrum analysis. However, the process requires extensive computation to inverse the correlation matrix, which creates major obstacle in real-world applications, especially when the dimensionality is high and matrix is close to singular. On this account, this paper proposes a fast approach to solve the inverse matrix recursively. The process utilizes the earlier part of the recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm, which includes correlation matrix definition and matrix inversion lemma. The order of computational complexity is reduced from O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) to O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) as compared to the direct calculation of the inverse matrix. Simulation results based on circular array antennas are presented to demonstrate that our approach outperforms regular MVDR computationally at a large scale. Circular array antennas were used as part of an integrated system for future hardware implementation.

articleTitle: Novel measurement technique for millimeter wave surface wave launchers
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A novel measurement technique for a surface wave launcher is presented. The measurement technique utilizes a wafer-probing station, and a custom-made field probe. A measurement setup and measured results are given for a Yagi-Uda launcher.

articleTitle: Adaptation of a cylindrical near-field system for radome characterization
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The performance of a radome degrades over time and it is therefore necessary to qualify a radome periodically to assure that it meets its original electrical performance specifications. This involves measuring the differential change in a number of antenna parameters in the presence of the radome. The variance in these parameters is then used as an indicator of the suitability of the radome for its designated application.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically coupled rectangular patch antenna for L-band operation: FDTD modeling
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Electromagnetically Coupled Patch Antenna (EMCP) appeared to be first discussed by Sabban [1]-[2] and since then it has been under careful investigations [3]-[9] because of its broadband operation together with simple structure. For example, Lee et al[3]-[5] experimented the effects of the parasitic patch sizes, dielectric superstartes and the distance between the patches on the behavior of the antenna very carefully. The conventional structure for EMCP is shown in Fig 1. In this paper a new designed structure for L-band operation is investigated using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. A fairly accurate model for coaxial probe fed is applied and the simulated input impedance and radiation patterns are compared with the measured results.

articleTitle: Root-of-area formula of electrical capacitance, for equivalent circuit of thermal conduction, from an HBT-IC through a GaAs substrate with temperature dependent conductivity
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Like the field computation of capacitance, thermal resistance from an ICs is normally done by simulating over a very large region of the device and substrate, in 3D and with very fine meshing. This is especially necessary in a temperature dependent substrate such as GaAs [1]. Through the root-of-area capacitance formula of the electrical equivalent, this paper shows that the tedious 3D fine meshing may be replaced by a simple equivalent circuit.

articleTitle: A new parabolic equation method for wave propagation modeling in lossy dielectric media
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents a new method based on the parabolic wave equation technique for modeling electromagnetic wave propagation in lossy dielectric media which can be applicable to many indoor propagation problems. We use transparent boundary condition with the split-step Padé approximation to solve parabolic wave equation. In order to prove the accuracy of the method, numerical results are compared with known exact solutions for plane wave oblique incidence onto a wall for both horizontal and vertical wave polarizations.

articleTitle: A micro-spring supported membrane for reconfigurable defected ground microstrip phase shifter
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A MEMS phase shifter is fabricated using a micro-spring supported membrane in the ground plane beneath a microstrip transmission line. As the membrane is actuated away from the substrate, phase shift in the transmission line signal occurs. Device performance is simulated and the results are compared with experiment. For a membrane measuring 1.6mm × 1mm fabricated in a ground plane aperture measuring 2mm × 2mm, a phase shift of 35.8° was measured at 18.5GHz, with only a −1.5dB change in measured S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> compared to the transmission line case.

articleTitle: Differential correlation with a linear antenna array for delay estimation in a CDMA system
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper we apply differential correlation — Multiple Signal Classification (DC-MUSIC) algorithm with a linear antenna array for delay estimation in an asynchronous CDMA system. Our analysis shows that the differential correlation matrix has a better structure when it is averaged over the different antennas. This results due to the interference and noise suppression capability of the antenna array. Computer simulation confirms that DC-MUSIC algorithm with multiple antennas provides better performance compared to its single-antenna counterpart. The multiple antenna DC-MUSIC algorithm also shows improved performance over the conventional MUSIC delay estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: Slot antenna for short pulse radiation
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: With the advances in digital communication the need for ultra wideband antennas (UWB) has increased. UWB antennas also have applications in medical diagnostics [1,2] and radar systems [3,4]. Examples of UWB antennas include loaded dipoles [5], loaded bowties, conical antennas [6,7] and V slot antenna. The magnetic slot antenna has been shown to have ultra wideband properties [8], however its performance degrades for very short pulses (pulse with duration less than 0.5 ns). In this paper we make use of Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimization method [9] to design an optimal (perhaps counterintuitive) design for the magnetic slot antenna. In this research the accuracy of method of moments (MoM) full-wave solutions and the robustness of the evolutionary optimization approach are combined.

articleTitle: Wireless test lab design considerations
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper describes a family of new measurement systems, termed “Test Labs”, designed to satisfy the certification requirements of the Cellular Telephone & Internet Association's (CTIA) mandated requirements for Over the Air Testing (OTA) for wireless subcriber stations. These test labs employ simultaneous dual-axis mechanical scanning and operate in both far-field and near-field modes over the 750MHz to 6 GHz frequency range. Operation can be extended to higher frequencies through the use of suitable sampling antennas. Test Lab facility configuration is detailed. Scanner layout and RF sampling antenna designs are discussed. Anechoic chamber characterization data is presented along with typical measured pattern and efficiency data for both broadbeam and directive AUT's. Measurement test times for various test scenarios are discussed.

articleTitle: High frequency GMI measurement of soft magnetic co-based ribbons
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, we present a method for extracting the magnetic parameters of soft magnetic Co-based alloy (Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">68.25</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4.5</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12.25</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>) in the high frequency regime (10MHz-2GHz). The magnetic sample (as-cast ribbon) is used as the conductor of a microstrip transmission line. The real and imaginary parts of series impedance (Z) of the line obtained from input impedance measurements, and a theoretical model based on the distributed parameters and the skin effect is used to extract the bulk transversal relative permeability. The effect of changing the applied external DC magnetic field is reported and the results show that the real parts of Z and propagation constant (γ) are very sensitive to the applied DC magnetic field. The model considers the geometrical contribution of the transmission line on the series impedance of the magnetic conductor (Co-based ribbon). In this work, we assume a real permeability, however the model can be readily used for extracting a complex transversal relative permeability (μ′<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tr</inf>–jμ″<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tr</inf>).

articleTitle: A 23 GHz transformer based antenna coupler for CMOS receiver front-end
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A 23GHz Front-end circuit with an on-chip integrated coupler, which is realizable in standard CMOS 0.18um process is proposed in this paper. The integrated coupler provides an alternative to bond wire connection between the antenna and the front-end. The LNA provides a gain of 17dB and noise figure of 5.8 dB. The mixer is optimized for maximum linearity and has an input referred 1dB compression point of +10dBm and a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order intercept point of 16dBm with conversion gain of 3dBm.

articleTitle: Adaptive array algorithm performance: Case studies in different environments
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Improvements in communications performance achievable by using adaptive array processors at mobile receivers are demonstrated using measured channel data. Performance of the least mean squares (LMS) and direct matrix inversion (DMI) algorithms is compared in rural, suburban, and urban environments. The ability of the algorithms to track channel changes in real environments is investigated by linking the algorithms' local performance with specific channel characteristics. It is seen that the LMS algorithm's performance varies widely with the environment, while the DMI algorithm has very consistent performance.

articleTitle: Extrapolation of data external to the measurement region: In the bi-polar scanning
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Among the near field-far field (NF-FF) transformation techniques, that employing the bi-polar scanning, proposed by Rahmat-Samii et al. in [1], is particularly attractive due to its peculiar characteristics. In such a scanning, the antenna under test (AUT) rotates axially, whereas the probe is attached to the end of an arm which rotates around an axis parallel to the AUT one. This allows one to collect the NF data on a grid of concentric rings and radial arcs (Fig. 1). The bi-polar scanning maintains all the advantages of the plane-polar one while providing a simple and cost-effective measurement system. In fact, since the arm is fixed at one point and the probe is attached at its end, the bending is constant and this allows to hold the planarity. Moreover, rotational movements are preferable to the linear ones, since rotating tables are more accurate than linear positioners. An efficient probe compensated NF-FF transformation using a bi-polar scanning has been recently developed by the authors in [2] by considering the AUT as enclosed in an oblate ellipsoid, a source modelling particularly suitable to deal with quasi-planar antennas. Such a technique is based on the theoretical results [3] concerning the nonredundant sampling representations of the electromagnetic (EM) fields for antennas enclosed in arbitrary convex domains with rotational symmetry and observed on surfaces having the same symmetry. It allows one to lower the number of needed NF data in a significant way with respect to the classical bi-polar scanning without losing the efficiency. An optimal sampling interpolation (OSI) algorithm has been applied to recover the plane-rectangular data from the bi-polar ones, thus enabling the use of the FFT in the NF-FF transformation.

articleTitle: Tunable branch-line hybrid circuit using electrical length variable quasi-distributed TFMS line
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In three-dimensional (3-D) MMICs, a me and er-like line is realized easily for in creasing the integration level and many devices such as metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors and FETs can be located on transmission lines. The circuits which use FETs have variable frequency response because the FETs have variable capacitance. In this paper, a transmission line composed of high impedance thin film microstrip (TFMS) lines and high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) which are realized easily by 3-D MMIC topology is described. This type of TFMS transmission line is called “electrical length variable quasi-distributed thin film microstrip (QD-TFMS) line”. Moreover, a tunable branch-line hybrid circuit in X band is realized by using the QD-TFMS lines. The relative tuning range of the branch-line hybrid circuit is up to about 20%. The intrinsic circuit area of the branch-line hybrid circuit is reduced to more than 70% smaller than that of conventional one.

articleTitle: Polarimetric bistatic GPR imaging and detection of landmines in the near field with the “Vampire Effect”
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: GPR images invariably suffer from a bandwidth restriction due to the low pass characteristics of the air-ground interface and are usually not clear enough to differentiate between what is a landmine and what is harmless clutter. The presence of clutter in the subsurface therefore contributes to high false alarm rates when landmine detection schemes are attempted. A landmine detection algorithm based on the vampire signature has been proposed and has been tested to verify its validity. The method involves the construction of a spatial filter from polarimetric data in order to enhance objects that exhibit the vampire effect while suppressing objects that do not. So far, the method has several significant limitations, most notably that the position and orientation of the symmetric scatters is strictly confined to be directly below the SAR path and that the target symmetry planes must include both antennas as well as the scan path. In this paper, the effects of off-centered measurements whereby the antennas are not necessarily contained in the target symmetry plane are discussed.

articleTitle: Improving the polarization of V-slot microstrip patch antenna with slotted ground
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The performance of V-slotted microstrip patch antenna is investigated, with additional edge slots on the ground plane. Placing two rectangular slots at the ground plane, parallel to patch shorter side, decreases the cross polarization level successfully, and improves the antenna gain at higher frequencies without affecting its bandwidth.

articleTitle: A distance-detecting method for planar near-field measurements using a printed ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost technique to measure the distance between a near-field probe and a planar antenna under test (AUT) is presented. This technique uses an unshielded printed ring resonator whose resonant frequency is shifted by varying its proximity to the AUT. The distance is derived from measured return loss of the ring resonator. The sensitivity of the resonant frequency with respect to the distance between the ring resonator and the AUT is more than 10 MHz/mm. This is compliant with the positioning accuracy requirements in near-field antenna measurements. Thus, it provides a convenient way to obtain the bound limit of z-positioning error. Such information can be used in AUT characterization based on the extraction of equivalent magnetic currents.

articleTitle: Numerical studies of EBG structures printed on CPW lines
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: One of the current topics in computational electromagnetics is the study of electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) structures using planar printed transmission lines. In fact, structures using microstrip-line circuits have been comprehensively applied in recent years. However, studies involving transmission lines using the coplanar waveguide (CPW) have not been commonly conducted. In this paper, a number of EBG structures constructed on the CPWs are studied by using a well-known numerical method, the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. Results show the band-stop filter behavior of these structures, and the computed results match generally well with the ones published in literature through solver validation. The proposed CPW EBG structures may be considered as alternatives to the conventional microstrip-line typed EBGs.

articleTitle: A new slot antenna fed by double excitation for wideband wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, a broadband slot antenna fed by double excitation is presented. The antenna structure design takes advantages of the slot coupling feeding technique and the slot antenna concept to improve the bandwidth. Using two excitations instead of one as used in conventional antennas to obtain double resonant frequencies closer, the bandwidth of the proposed antenna was improved and a good performance in terms of bandwidth and gain was achieved. The proposed antenna was designed, fabricated and tested at 5.8 GHz. With this approach, a measured bandwidth of ∼ 28.5% (1.6 GHz) was achieved. The simulated and measured return loss and radiation pattern were compared and discussed.

articleTitle: Strategic miniaturization of the broadband “Dark Eyes” antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The general motivation behind the work presented in the paper is the need for broadband antennas for pulsed biological sensing centered in the microwave range [1], [3]. We continue our study of a particular antenna design (“inverse bowtie” or the “Dark Eyes” antenna) which takes advantage of constant resistive loading in combination with favorable antenna geometry to minimize reflections from antenna ends [2], [3], [4].

articleTitle: Recent advances in neural based time domain EM modeling and simulation
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, the recent neural network (NN) approaches to time domain electromagnetic (EM)-based modeling are summarized. Fast and accurate passive EM models can be created using three recent methods, i.e., (equivalent circuit and neural network) EC-NN, (state space equation and neural network) SSE-NN and (equivalent circuit, state space equation and neural network) EC-SSE-NN. Those methods are based on combined equivalent circuit and/or state space theory. Each of the combined modeling techniques has its own usage depending on the availability of the equivalent circuit and user-desired accuracy. In order to develop a nonlinear transient model to be used together with passive components in time domain EM-based simulation, the adjoint dynamic neural network (ADNN)-based modeling technique can be utilized. Through accurate and fast time domain EM-based neural models of passive/active components, we enable consideration of EM effects in high-frequency and high-speed computer-aided design (CAD), including component's geometrical/physical parameters as optimization variables. Examples of EM modeling of embedded passives and their use in time domain EM-based simulation and design are presented.

articleTitle: Time-domain passive macromodels of S-parameter based EM subnetworks
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Passive time-domain macromodeling of EM subnetworks and high-speed modules characterized by S-parameters has generated immense interest during the recent years. This paper presents an efficient algorithm for addressing passivity of macromodels of S-parameter based subnetworks. New approaches for fast passivity verification and compensation are described. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Enabling electromagnetic applications of negative-refractive-index transmission-line metamaterials part II
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The 1-Dimensional (1-D) metamaterial phase-shifting lines presented in [1] can be used to develop compact and broadband, non-radiating, metamaterial feed-networks for antenna arrays. These can be used to replace conventional TL-based feed-networks, which can be bulky and narrowband. For series-fed arrays, the proposed metamaterial feed-networks have the advantage of being compact in size, therefore eliminating the need for conventional TL meander lines. In addition, the metamaterial feed-networks are more broadband when compared to conventional TL feed-networks, which enables series-fed broadside arrays to experience less beam squint when operated away from the design frequency. For parallel-fed arrays, the proposed metamaterial feed-networks have the potential to significantly reduce the size of the feed networks by completely collapsing the traditionally used TL-based binary tree feed-network.

articleTitle: Indoor propagation of wireless LAN signals in a hospital and electromagnetic compatibilty implications
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The rapid growth of wireless communication associated with usage of cellular phones, PDAs, pagers and other wireless devices has been phenomenal. Yet such growth has not occurred within healthcare, in part due to concerns about electromagnetic interference (EMI) potentially causing malfunction of life-critical medical equipment. Interference with critical-care medical equipment can threaten patient safety [1, 2, 3], and as a result many hospitals have banned cellular telephones, and other wireless sources.

articleTitle: RF interference supression using array beamforming
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In today's EM environment jamming or interference due to own communication sets occurs due to Electromagnetic interference (EMI). In civil communication/ installations and particularly in the armed forces, there has been an ever increasing density and deployment of electronic systems. It is known that the EM spectrum around any platform/ installation is dependent on the radiations emanating from it. Thus, cohabitation of sensitive electronic systems near transmitter aerials has become a major challenge to the designer.

articleTitle: Correct orientation of dipole elements for reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper shows how to compute precisely the orientation of the dipole elements at the surface of a reflectarray. The orientation is obtained as the projection of far-field E of the pyramidal feed horn onto the plane of the reflectarray. It is shown that this orientation is not uniform across the reflectarray. The difference between the orientation at an arbitrary point of the reflectary and the orientation at the centre of the reflectarray, is maximum at points in the inter-cardinal planes. For a square reflectarray of 12 cm per side, illuminated by a 26.5 GHz pyramidal feed horn with its phase centre located 13.5 cm away from the centre of the reflectarray, the difference can be up to about ±5°.

articleTitle: Signal enhancement in a near-field MIMO environment through adaptivity on transmit
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Many methods have been developed and are continuing to evolve in recent years, to enhance reception of signals in a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) environment [1,2]. For mobile communication, the development of a methodology that mitigates the deleterious effects of multipath fading, near-field scatterers (buildings, trees, platforms), etc. is necessary for improved reception. To achieve such enhancements, the authors believe that transmit/receive configurations with spatial diversity are required as shown in Figure 1. Unfortunately, the small footprint of a mobile receiver precludes spatial diversity. In contrast, spatial diversity on transmit is obtainable at a base station, if that station has multiple antennas and the signals being fed to each one of the transmitting antennas corresponding to a particular receiver are weighted. So this paper addresses the of what can be done in terms of adaptivity on transmit so as to enhance the field strength of the signal at a pre-specified receiver while simultaneously minimizing the reception signal strength at the remaining receivers. In this way, the transmitted signals would be received essentially at the designated receiver while it would be canceled at the other locations. By providing spatial diversity on transmit it is possible to mitigate the effects of multipath fading, as the directed energy from the transmitted antennas, would combine vectorially at the selected receiving antenna element either to produce a maximum or a minimum.

articleTitle: Low actuation voltage ground plane membranes for a frequency agile microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A frequency agile microstrip patch antenna is presented. A micromachined membrane is used as the ground plane below the antenna patch. Actuation of this membrane away from the patch introduces an air gap between the substrate and the ground plane. Control of the air gap thickness, enables control of the antenna's resonant frequency. Thereby, enabling this narrowband antenna to operate over a wide frequency band. Ensemble simulations and experimental results are presented. Measurements showed control of antenna resonant frequency from 16.8GHz to 17.82GHz (approximately 6% variation) for the ground plane membrane deflecting from 0μm to 138μm.

articleTitle: Design of an E-probe proximity fed triangular patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Microstrip antennas are attractive for various applications: easy to fabricate and integrate, compact, well-known and controlled. Even so, they are inescapably narrow band, which remains a definite drawback for numerous systems emerging, for example in communication and sensor areas. Nowadays, the need of broadband antennas is constantly growing. That is why many solutions are studied to increase the microstrip antenna's bandwidth. Using a probe of a specific shape to feed the antenna is a particularly interesting solution. Previous studies have shown promising results, using an L-shaped or an F-shaped probe with a rectangular or triangular patch antenna mounted on a finite ground plane, using a low permittivity thick substrate [1, 2, 3, 4]. The maximum bandwidth obtained was 64 % (VSWR < 2). In this paper, we present a new design of an E-probe fed triangular patch antenna. Thus a parametric study has been achieved showing the influence on the impedance matching by varying the height of the patch and the height of one of the horizontal strips. The results allow to find an optimal design, which has been fabricated and compared to the simulated one.

articleTitle: Effect of antenna correlation on the MMSE multiuser detector performance in DS-CDMA systems
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, the effects of correlation between antenna elements on the performance of direct sequence code division multiple access (DS-CDMA) systems were investigated over frequency selective Rayleigh fading channels. Performances of two well known linear minimum mean square error (MMSE) receiver structures of reverse link are compared with different correlation levels. Three different correlation models are studied to see the sensitivity of the overall system to a specific channel correlation model. A new approximate method is devised to obtain the average bit error probability (BER) curves.

articleTitle: A proposed measurement method to extract the transmission and reflection properties of a periodic structure
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Periodic structures have always been interesting for researchers in electromagnetic area. A typical example is the frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) that may be used in antenna radoms or sub-reflector of multi-feed reflector systems.

articleTitle: Dielectric spectroscopy of breast tissue — Measurement and permittivity models
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The knowledge of dielectric properties of breast tissue in a wide frequency range of 0.1 to 20 GHz forms the foundation for a variety of novel microwave techniques for breast cancer detection [1,2,3]. In collaboration, the Universities of Calgary and Wisconsin-Madison are building an extensive database of breast tissue dielectric properties for further advances of microwave technologies for breast cancer detection and treatment [1,5,7].

articleTitle: Modeling, design and analysis of the two movable plate nitride loaded MEMS variable capacitor
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The modeling, design and analysis of the MEMS variable capacitor having two movable plates loaded with a Nitride layer is proposed. A trench in the silicon substrate underneath the capacitor is used to decrease the parasitic capacitance. The use of an insulation dielectric layer on the bottom plate of the MEMS capacitor prevents a short circuit and allows the top plate of nickel to relax on the nitride layer. The addition of the nitride layer results in increasing the capacitor's tuning range and eliminating the sticktion. Experimental, theoretical and analytical results are presented. The measured tuning range is found to be 280% at 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Effect of printed circuit board vias on high speed signal propagation
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Conventional printed circuit boards made of popular FR4 material are being increasingly used for the transportation of very high speed digital data. Experiments have demonstrated successful usage at speeds of 3.125 Giga bits per second (Gbps). Deployment at speeds of 10 Gbps is also feasible over a limited trace length. A primary deterrent to the usage of printed circuit board traces has been losses in both copper as well as the dielectric. This leads to both attenuation and dispersion. Advances in active device technology have enabled the use of pre-emphasis techniques in drivers, and equalization in receivers. These techniques help overcome signal distortion and are becoming common place in most 10 Gbps modules. As such, the printed circuit board traces are often implemented as a straight coplanar waveguide over a very short length. The active components are also designed for surface mount operation to facilitate this. For pushing the envelope further, the need for complex interconnects between different high speed modules becomes necessary. On high density multi-layered printed circuit boards, routing as straight coplanar waveguide or microstrip traces would become impossible, and the need for stripline routing becomes necessary. In such situations, the need to use vias to interconnect printed traces on different layers becomes inevitable. Printed Circuit Board vias, in their common implementation represent a non-uniform transmission medium and introduce a discontinuity in the signal path. This discontinuity is quite complex and can be difficult to overcome using existing pre-emphasis and equalization techniques. For this reason, much work has been devoted to the understanding of wave propagation through via structures and to develop techniques to reduce the effect of this discontinuity [1]. This paper makes a contribution in this direction through the use of simulation tools.

articleTitle: Thick volume hologram for microwave frequency band: Design, fabrication, and test
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A method is proposed for the fabrication of a thick volume hologram for applications in the microwave frequency band. Artificial dielectric technology is used to realize the transverse modulation of refractive index. Design guidelines and principles are explained. A prototype is fabricated based on the proposed method and tested to demonstrate its validity. The efficiency of the prototype is approximately 70% in the transmission mode that is typical of “thick phase holograms”. To the best knowledge of authors, this is the first time that a thick volume hologram is fabricated in the microwave frequency band.

articleTitle: A novel planar broadband balun
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper a novel planar balun was designed. The balun consists of a CPW-slotline T-junction with a CPW-slotline transition on either side of the T. One of the transitions is flipped so that an 180° phase shift is created at the output. The phase balance is maintained over a 31.5 GHz bandwidth, from 445 MHz to 32 GHz. The useful bandwidth is limited to 10 GHz due to return loss. The balun was simulated using Momentum and Ensemble, and was fabricated using Phillips' OMMIC ED02AH process.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic band gap-slot antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, we analyze EBG-Slot antennas using a method that we have previously developed. This method allows predicting phenomena that we could not predict by usual methods. We give FDTD results of radiation patterns and matching of these structures.

articleTitle: A novel electromagnetic bandgap groundplane design
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper describes a novel groundplane that could be classified as a defected groundplane; however, instead of introducing holes (defects), the groundplane is grooved. A gridwork of grooves works with a dielectric layer above it to create regions of alternate high and low permittivity that form a periodic pattern, similar to designs with dielectric posts. A deep and wide bandgap can be obtained by optimizing the geometric dimensions. There is a trade-off for manufacturing since the design does not require any vias but does require machining of the groundplane.

articleTitle: Interference rejection by adaptive antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper addresses the use of adaptive antennas to reject interference and to enhance the performance of wireless communication systems. It presents a simulated performance of an adaptive antenna system operating in Rayleigh and Rician fading environments in the presence of multiple co-channel interferers. In addition, the rate at which the adaptive parameters need to be derived and the role of the length of a training sequence on system performance are investigated.

articleTitle: Left-handed behaviour in a ferrite-filled, antisymmetrically-biased rectangular waveguide phase shifter
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Over the last few years, artificial materials (metamaterials) demonstrating so-called left-handed behaviour have been reported [1,2]. Left-handed materials have a peculiar property in that their group velocity is negative with respect to their phase velocity. During the course of an investigation into a new rectangular waveguide phase shifter, it was discovered that the ferrite also supports left-handed propagation, albeit over a very limited range of frequencies. Left-handedness thus also appears to be possible in natural materials, not just in artificial ones. In this paper, the salient features of the ferrite medium inside the phase shifter are presented, and the longitudinal component of the Poynting vector is examined throughout the guide's cross-section at multiple frequencies.

articleTitle: Simple formula of mutual impedance of patch antennas constructed from variable separation of the near field and radiation pattern of the far field
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Knowledge of mutual coupling between antennas is of much importance for the design of practical antenna arrays of finite size. This paper constructs a formula for mutual impedance between patch antennas based on the physics of the static near field coupling and of the far field radiation couplings, i.e., the near and far asymptotes. The two asymptotes are then combined to form a synthetic asymptote [1], of separated variables of the center-to-center distance r and the azimuth angle ϕ. Only 12 coefficients are to be determined by matching with a full wave analysis with commercial software, such as IE3D. Our formula is complete with no restriction on the detailed structures of patch, feed and substrate.

articleTitle: Patch antennas feed modeling for method of moments
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Inaccurate feed modeling in the antenna design and analysis is one of the main sources errors in the Method of Moments (MoM) analysis. In this paper we present a new feed modeling for MoM with the well-known RWG basis functions [3]. The proposed model is a generalization of the well-known delta-gap voltage source adapted to patch antennas [1,2]. The RWG basis functions used in this paper — and widely used in method of moments analysis — are now recognized as one of the first vector (“edge”) elements to be used in computational electromagnetic. The feed modeling presented here can be easily generalized to other type of basis functions. The validity of the this model is demonstrated by means of two examples and the results are compared with ones obtained from recent studies [6] which use Ansoft Ensemble to obtain the antenna parameters. Good agreement between the results of two methods is achieved. MATLAB 6.5 is used for simulations.

articleTitle: Artificial magnetic conductor using split ring resontrs and its applications
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In the recent decade, realization of the perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) has been extensively studied since PMC can replace the perfect electric conductor (PEC) in many microwave applications and obtain the attractive results as well as the compact structures [1-5]. For example, a reflector using the PEC must be positioned quarter-wavelength from an aperture-coupled antenna, but the low-profile antenna is possible when using the reflector of PMC [5].

articleTitle: Comparison of immersion liquids for tissue sensing adaptive radar
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Tissue sensing adaptive radar (TSAR) imaging has been proposed for the early detection of breast tumours. This technology takes advantage of the differences in electrical properties of normal and malignant tissues. In this paper, we work towards practical implementation by evaluating various immersion liquids in which the breast and sensors are placed.

articleTitle: Shaped slot waveguide applied to beam scanning antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Slots waveguide arrays are very useful in microwave applications, especially in microwave communications and radar systems. The number of applications could be explain by good performances featuring by the slots waveguide antenna, specially in terms of cross polarization and very low losses up to millimeters waves bands.

articleTitle: PAASoM: A simulation tool in Matlab for phased array analysis
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A simulation tool has been developped using Matlab [1] to analyse the radiation characteristics of phased array antennas. This program is called PAASoM, standing for Phased Array Antenna Software in Matlab. Matlab has been chosen for its capability of data plotting and the multiple mathematical functions that are already defined. The software program PAASoM allows the studies of arrays of different geometries and lattices, and with the possibility of weighting each element in phase and magnitude. The elements can be grouped in sub-arrays, and each sub-array can have its own phase weigthing. The array factor can be calculated in one or several planes as a function of a parameter given by the user. This parameter can be the number of bits of the phase shifters, the scanning angle, the frequency or the azimuth angle indicating the plane of calculation. Error analysis can also be carried out. The error can be on the magnitude, the phase or the position of each element.

articleTitle: A wide band 3dB hybrid/hopfer coupler
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A three section, 3dB edge-coupled coupler is designed and simulated to operate in the frequency range from 6GHz to 18GHz. The center section is a regular Hopfer Coupler, and the two outer sections are microstrips with upper shields. The coupler is simulated using various circuit and em simulators to achieve ±.5 dB amplitude balance in the frequency band of interest. A low dielectric (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 2.2) is used to track the phase velocities of the even and odd modes. Dimensions are optimized to achieve the required amplitude balance and the bandwidth while avoiding various resonances. To help identify various resonances, simulations were performed below 6 and above 18GHz as well. The optimized dimensions seem to respond well to possible manufacturing tolerances. To achieve the required coupling, BW and the amplitude balance, a poorer return loss was tolerated.

articleTitle: Analysis of gate modulation in nanoscale field effect transistors using an equivalent substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) model
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) model has been used to analyze the gate modulation of field effect transistors (FET) with a molecular channel of nanoscale material. By neglecting quantum mechanical effects and by treating nanoscale material as a “rigid” substrate, static electric field distribution inside the FET channel is analyzed. Numerical results show that the modulated electric fields near the interface between the FET channel and the gate insulator vary with dielectric constant of nanoscale material. Moreover, we found that, regardless of channel material and insulator thickness, the electric field penetrating inside the FET channel decreases in a similar way with the distance from the interface. This paper provides useful information for the detailed calculation of I-V curves and for the design of nanoscale FETs.

articleTitle: Wideband circular polarized microstrip antennas with V-slot
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: A 4-element sequentially rotated microstrip patches with V shape slot cut on each element is presented as a candidate for broadband circular polarized microstrip antenna sub array. The simulated results show, excellent axial ratio and stable gain within the wide (36.5%) impedance bandwidth of the V-slotted elements.

articleTitle: Parametric study of angular and radial probe positioning errors in a large spherical near-field automotive antenna test system
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: The testing of modern automotive antennas is often accomplished by using spherical near-field test facilities. This paper presents sensitivity analysis data for errors introduced in the probe position of such a test system. The purpose of this study is to establish mechanical design goals for the gantry structure required in the implementation of the probe positioning system. Far-field error levels are calculated to demonstrate the effect of the probe positioning anomalies.

articleTitle: MM-wave patch yagi fed cylindrical dielectric lens antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Wide angle scanning antenna is essential for many mm-wave applications such as broadband wireless communications, automobile radars and imaging radars [1-3]. An excellent design is given in [2] using a simple spherical lens antenna to launch 33 pencil-beams to achieve 180° scan coverage. This paper extends this design concept to launch scanning fan-beams by using cylindrical lens between two parallel conductor plates. The measurement agrees very well with the simulations, and a gain of 11.5dB with E- and H-plane beamwidth of 4.9° and 72° is achieved at 30GHz. The demonstrated patch-yagi/cylindrical Rexolite lens antenna can be easily extended to launch multiple beams to cover 180° coverage, and therefore well suited for either single or scanning fan-beam applications, such as aircraft landing systems [4].

articleTitle: Time-domain channel estimation and performance evaluation of a MIMO-OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: This paper presents a simplified channel estimation technique for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems with multiple input, multiple output (MIMO) antenna structure. The estimation technique is presented both in the frequency and time domains. Quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) modulation technique is used to modulate the transmitted data. To ensure low computational complexity, time domain estimated channel information is considered to evaluate the performance of the OFDM system in terms of symbol error rate (SER). For both channel estimation and performance evaluation, simulation results are presented for two-transmit and one-receive antenna configuration in the two-ray Rayleigh fading channel environment.

articleTitle: Wireless-local-area-network deployment issues in hospitals: Capacity, coverage & electromagnetic compatibility
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Healthcare is an important industry that touches most, if not all, of us. The wireless communication revolution can potentially provide medical staff with rapid, bedside access to medical information. Rapid access not only improves healthcare delivery, but can also reduce medical errors, which have been estimated to cause up to 100,000 patient deaths each year in US hospitals alone [1]. Given the potential benefits of using wireless informatics in hospitals, some hospitals are currently using wireless local area network (WLAN) informatics systems, and many hospitals would like to. The potentially-enormous benefit of WLAN informatics comes with the concern that electromagnetic interference (EMI) from radio-frequency (RF) sources might cause critical-care medical equipment to malfunction. There have been many previous reports of medical device malfunction due to EMI [2,3]. Many EMI sources were described, including, although relatively rarely [2], wireless LANs.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit model for photonic bandgap microstrip lines with ground plane perforations
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Microstrip transmission lines with periodically etched ground plane perforations act as photonic bandgap structures, and have proven useful in the design of devices and antennas at microwave frequencies. In order to obtain the exact characteristics of the structure, a time consuming full-wave simulation is usually required. In this paper, an equivalent circuit model for structures with rectangular ground plane perforations is proposed. Once initial circuit parameters are established, the model can be used to easily obtain the structure response for different periods and lengths of the etched perforations. The equivalent circuit, full-wave simulation, and measurement results are compared for several structures, showing a good agreement.

articleTitle: Integration of an FDTD analysis of lossy multiconductor transmission lines within a general-purpose circuit simulator
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: In this paper, a multiport circuit model for a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) analysis of the multiconductor transmission line equations is derived. The multiport model enables easy integration of a lossy transmission-line network within a general-purpose nonlinear circuit simulator. The model can be viewed as a link between a distributed-system analysis method, FDTD, and a lumped-element network solver, the circuit simulator. The multiport circuit model consists of resistors and dependent current sources which are updated at every time step by the FDTD algorithm. The approach is capable of dealing with distributed sources, as well as lumped sources. The analysis of a two-conductor transmission line with nonlinear terminations is presented as an application of this approach.

articleTitle: Error filtering in the NF-FF transformation with cylindrical scanning
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Measurement techniques in the antenna near-field (NF) region have a significant role in the evaluation of far-field (FF) patterns. In fact, for electrically large antennas the required size of the conventional FF range becomes prohibitively large. Moreover, NF facilities provide a controlled and secure environment, and all weather capability. Among the NF-FF transformation techniques, that employing the cylindrical scanning (Fig. 1) is particularly attractive. In fact, at the cost of a moderate increase in the analytical and computational complication with respect to the planar scannings, it allows the reconstruction of the antenna complete radiation pattern save for the zones surrounding the spherical poles.

articleTitle: Enabling electromagnetic applications of negative-refractive-index transmission-line metamaterials part I
publicationTitle: 2004 10th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics and URSI Conference
abstract: Metamaterials are artificial periodic media with unusual electromagnetic properties. The size of their unit cells is much smaller than the incident wavelength, thus allowing one to define effective media parameters such a permittivity ε, a permeability μ, and a refractive index n. In this work, “left-handed” metamaterials are considered for which their permittivity and permeability are both negative. These metamaterials exhibit backward-wave propagation characteristics and therefore a negative index of refraction as was predicted in the visionary work of Victor Veselago [1]. Such “left-handed” or “Negative-Refractive-Index” (NRI) media were first implemented using bulk periodic arrays of thin wires to synthesize negative permittivity and split-ring resonators to synthesize a negative permeability [2]. However, the NRI medium presented in [2] relies on resonant elements to synthesize the negative permeability thus leading to narrow bandwidths and high transmission losses. More recently, a completely planar approach for synthesizing NRI media without resonant elements was proposed in [3],[4]. The 2-Dimensional (2-D) NRI structure presented in [3],[4] was realized by periodically loading a planar network of printed transmission lines (TL) with series capacitors and shunt inductors in a dual-TL (high-pass) configuration. The 2-D NRI medium was subsequently interfaced with a commensurate conventional dielectric, leading to the first experimental demonstration of focusing from a NRI metamaterial [4], [5]. More recently, a 3-region lens arrangement was used to observe focusing beyond the diffraction limit [6]-[7] as was predicted by J.B. Pendry [9]. A similar TL approach was followed by Itoh and Caloz and led to interesting structures and circuits [10], [11]. Moreover, intriguing and useful anisotropic transmission-line metamaterials have been reported by Balmain et al. in [12]. In addition, some of the first FDTD simulations of NRI media have been reported in the pioneering work of R. Ziolkowski et al. in [13]. Further developments in the general area of Metamaterials can be found in two recent special issues: The October 2003 issue of the IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation (Guest Editors R. Ziolkowski and N. Engheta) and the April 2003 issue of Optics Express (vol. 11, No. 7, Guest Editor J.B. Pendry).
